title: Chern number difference as the signed sum of conical crossings in finite Hermitian homotopies
difficulty_reason: H2: the integer Chern-number difference is not a consequence of generic conical degeneracies alone. The author localises the Riesz-projector Berry curvature to the finitely many selected-band crossings, separates the smooth lower bundle from the singular rank-one part, reduces the compressed two-dimensional Taylor model to Pauli flux by orientation-preserving coordinates and SU(2)/SO(3) conjugation, and combines controlled remainder limits with integrality. This spectral-topological localisation and orientation-dependent charge calculation exceeds a routine degree or Sard exercise; prior technical projector and curvature estimates are explicitly attributed as inputs, without assistant proof completion or correctness certification.

core_obligations: H0,H1 are smooth T2-to-finite-Hermitian-space maps and lambda_n(Hj)<lambda_(n+1)(Hj) at every xi for j=0,1, with 1<=n<=N-1.

H is a smooth fixed-endpoint homotopy whose crossings between exactly the selected pair are conical in the original Definition1; the two-dimensional eigenspace has precise multiplicity2 and invertible cone matrix.
Preserve the finite crossing set zeta1,...,zetaK, chirality sign det A_k and endpoint rank-n bundles V0,V1. Exact conclusion is c1(V1)-c1(V0)=sum_k sgn det A_k.

Retain the complete Section5 author argument, including lower-band additivity, local smooth-frame model, stated projector derivative errors, oriented Gram-Schmidt/SU2 reduction, expanding ellipse flux, O(r+delta) limit and integrality.
Other-band simplicity, infinite-dimensional operators, a global dynamical propagation estimate and a quantitative Dirac approximation are not added assumptions or conclusions.
Theorem1 fixed-endpoint density follows through old2049/extension/cutoffs and is related supporting material, not a second new count.
